content: Ketoconazole is a medication used to treat specific skin conditions, such as seborrheic dermatitis, a type of dandruff. This condition is believed to result from a fungal infection (Malassezia furfur) affecting the skin or scalp, leading to dry, flaky skin (scales) on areas such as the scalp, face, ears, chest, or upper back. How to Use Ketoconazole: Before starting treatment, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Follow the instructions each time you refill the medication. This medication is for external use only on the scalp and skin. Clean and thoroughly dry the affected area before application. Wash your hands before and after applying the medication. Apply the medication to the affected skin and a small portion of the surrounding normal skin as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. The duration of treatment depends on your response and is usually around two weeks. Do not apply more frequently than prescribed. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, or mouth. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Use the medication consistently to achieve the best results. Do not wash the treated area for at least three hours after application. Side Effects: Common side effects may include burning, redness, or dryness of the treated skin. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to ketoconazole or other azole antifungals (e.g., clotrimazole, econazole, miconazole) or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, use this medication only if clearly needed. Consult your doctor for advice. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Discuss with your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone swallows this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center right away (U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222). Storage: Store at room temperature. This product is flammable; keep it away from open flames. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused products. Important Notes: This medication should only be used for your current condition and not for other skin conditions unless directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Ketoconazole is a potent antifungal agent that inhibits the synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of fungal cell membranes. It is not recommended as a first-line treatment and should only be used when other effective antifungal therapies are unavailable or not tolerated. The potential benefits must outweigh the risks, including hepatotoxicity (liver damage), which has been reported with oral use, sometimes leading to fatalities or liver transplantation. It is contraindicated in certain conditions and with specific medications due to the risk of serious interactions, such as QT prolongation and life-threatening arrhythmias. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
